skill.name: wordpress-router
skill.description: Classify WordPress repositories and route coding agents to the right workflow for plugins, themes, block themes, REST APIs, WP-CLI, testing, performance, and security tasks.
skill.summary: Routes WordPress codebase tasks to the correct specialized workflow after project triage.
skill.author: Automattic

security_audit.summary: The skill contains one hardcoded Node triage command that executes a local project classification script. The remaining static findings are Markdown inline code references to files, fields, and output values, not command execution. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs agents to run a Node triage script.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the command hardcoded and require normal tool approval before execution. Document what the script reads and avoid passing user-controlled arguments.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 25 instructs the agent to run a hardcoded Node script for WordPress project triage. The command has no user-controlled arguments, but it is still real external command execution that should require normal approval.
SKILL.md line 32 uses backticks around a Markdown file path that the agent should read. It is documentation for locating a reference file, not shell execution.
SKILL.md line 44 uses backticks around the literal triage output value `kind: unknown`. It does not contain a command or executable instruction.
SKILL.md line 45 lists WordPress-related filenames and directories in Markdown backticks. These are inspection targets, not shell commands or dynamic execution.

content.value_statement: WordPress repositories can contain plugins, themes, blocks, full sites, or core checkouts with different workflows. This skill classifies the project and routes Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to the right WordPress task path.
actual_capabilities: Runs a WordPress project triage command to classify the repository type.
Identifies plugin, theme, block theme, block plugin, WordPress core, full site, and Gutenberg repository contexts.
Routes tasks to workflow areas such as blocks, theme.json, REST API, WP-CLI, testing, performance, and security.
Checks available tooling such as PHP, Composer, Node, @wordpress/scripts, PHPUnit, Playwright, and wp-env.
Applies guardrails for version constraints, repository conventions, and ambiguous routing decisions.
limitations: Requires access to the repository root to classify the project accurately.
Some routed workflows require separate WordPress skills that may not be installed.
Some verification paths depend on local tools such as WP-CLI, Composer, npm, or wp-env.
Ambiguous repositories may still require one clarification question from the user.

use_cases.title: Start a WordPress plugin task
use_cases.description: Classify the repository and route work on hooks, settings pages, activation hooks, uninstall logic, or REST endpoints.

use_cases.title: Handle theme and block theme changes
use_cases.description: Identify classic theme, block theme, theme.json, template, and pattern work before choosing the next workflow.

use_cases.title: Prepare safe repository verification
use_cases.description: Detect available lint, test, build, PHPUnit, Playwright, and wp-env tooling before recommending validation commands.

prompt_templates.title: Classify this WordPress repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wordpress-router to classify this repository and tell me which WordPress workflow should handle it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage before any code changes

prompt_templates.title: Route my plugin change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wordpress-router for this WordPress repo. I need to add a settings page and REST endpoint. Identify the repo kind and route the work.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the right theme workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wordpress-router to inspect this theme repository. Decide whether this is a classic theme or block theme, then recommend the next workflow and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan validation for a mixed WordPress site
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wordpress-router on this full WordPress site repo. Classify the strongest project signals, route each requested change, and list the safest verification commands.

output_examples.input: Use wordpress-router on this repository before we edit a custom block.
output_examples.output: The repository appears to be a WordPress block plugin. Route the work to block development, then verify with the existing build and test scripts if present.

output_examples.input: This repo has theme.json and templates. What workflow should handle it?
output_examples.output: This is likely a WordPress block theme. Use the block theme workflow and verify changes against theme.json, templates, patterns, and supported WordPress versions.

output_examples.input: The triage result says kind unknown.
output_examples.output: Inspect common WordPress signals such as composer.json, package.json, style.css, block.json, theme.json, and wp-content. Ask whether the target is a plugin, theme, or full site if the signals remain unclear.

best_practices: Run project triage before choosing a WordPress workflow.
Prefer the repository's existing lint, test, build, and package manager commands.
Confirm target WordPress and PHP versions when the repository does not show them.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every WordPress repository is a plugin.
Do not recommend WP-CLI or wp-env commands before checking whether the tooling exists.
Do not skip clarification when the repository kind and user intent conflict.

faq.question: What does this skill do first?
faq.answer: It runs or uses project triage to classify the WordPress repository before routing the task.

faq.question: Can it edit WordPress code by itself?
faq.answer: It is a router skill. It selects the right workflow and guardrails for later code changes.

faq.question: Which WordPress project types can it recognize?
faq.answer: It covers plugins, mu-plugins, classic themes, block themes, block plugins, full sites, WordPress core, and Gutenberg repositories.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require WP-CLI?
faq.answer: Not for all routing. Some downstream workflows or verification steps may require WP-CLI if the repository supports it.

faq.question: What happens when routing is ambiguous?
faq.answer: The skill asks one focused question about whether the project is a plugin, theme, or full site repository.
